requirements.text: The system must model underwriting as an explicit, ordered multi-stage workflow with these stages: intake, document extraction, financial spreading, risk grading, memo drafting, policy compliance check, tiered approval, closing.

Each deal must carry an explicit current-stage value, and stage transitions must be constrained so a deal can only advance along the defined workflow order (or be returned to an earlier stage for rework).
A pipeline board must display every active deal with its current stage and stage status, so users can see where each deal stands at a glance.
Intake and document extraction must accept the formats applications currently arrive in: email content and spreadsheet files.
The system must store uploaded source artifacts (emails, spreadsheets, financial statements) per deal and retain them for later citation and audit.
An intake triage agent must classify each incoming request (e.g. request type / product / suitability for underwriting).
The intake triage agent must identify and flag missing required documents on an incoming request.
The intake triage agent must recommend routing of each request to the correct analyst queue.
The system must maintain analyst work queues that deals can be routed into and worked from.
A financial spreading agent must extract figures from borrower financial statements into a standard spread template.
The financial spreading agent must attach a source reference to every extracted number, showing where in the borrower's statements the figure came from.
The standard spread template must be a defined, structured schema of line items so spreads are consistent across deals and machine-readable by the ratio engine.
Every spread line item must persist its provenance (source document, location within the document, and extracted raw value) alongside the accepted value.
Deterministic, non-agent logic must compute the credit ratios DSCR, leverage, and current ratio from the accepted spread.
Deterministic, non-agent logic must assign the risk grade from a transparent, inspectable rubric.
Ratio and risk-grade computations must be reproducible and explainable: the system must be able to show the inputs, the formula/rubric rule applied, and the resulting value.

The specific risk-grading rubric — grade scale, the ratio/qualitative thresholds, and how they map to a grade — is not defined in the evidence and must be supplied before grading can be implemented as intended.
A credit memo agent must draft the underwriting memo for a deal.
The credit memo draft must cite the specific ratios, spread figures, and policy rules it relied on, with those citations traceable back to the stored values.
A policy compliance agent must review every drafted memo against lending policy, covering at minimum concentration limits, prohibited industries, and loan-to-value caps.
The policy compliance agent must raise written exceptions describing each policy violation it finds.

Lending policy rules (concentration limits, prohibited industry list, loan-to-value caps) must be stored as configurable, versioned data rather than hard-coded, and the system must ship with a documented default rule set since no bank policy document was supplied.
Concentration-limit evaluation must aggregate across the active portfolio (not just the deal under review), so the system must support portfolio-level exposure aggregation by the relevant dimensions.
Policy exceptions must be persisted on the deal with their status (open, accepted/waived, resolved) and the named human who dispositioned them.
A portfolio Q&A agent must let credit officers ask natural-language questions across active deals, such as "show me all deals above $500k with DSCR under 1.2".
Portfolio Q&A answers must be grounded in stored deal data and must not assert figures that are not retrievable from that data.
The portfolio Q&A agent must be read-only: it may query deal data but may not mutate deals, stages, or decisions.
Portfolio Q&A results must respect the asking user's role-based visibility scope, so a user cannot see deals through Q&A that they could not see directly.
Each agent must operate under a narrow mandate limited to its stage; agents must not perform work assigned to another agent or to deterministic logic.
All agent output must be persisted as a proposal/draft in a pending state that is distinct from accepted deal data, and only human-accepted output may feed downstream stages.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: a credit analyst may approve deals up to $250k.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: a senior credit officer may approve deals up to $1M.
Approvals must be tiered by exposure: deals above $1M must be approved by a credit committee.
The system must derive the required approval tier from the deal's exposure amount and refuse an approval submitted by a user whose authority level is below that tier.

Credit-committee approval mechanics for deals above $1M are undefined: whether it requires a quorum of multiple named approvers, a recorded committee vote, or a single chair recording the committee's decision. This changes the approval data model and UI.
No agent may approve, decline, or advance a deal past an approval step; approval-step transitions must be executable only by an authenticated human.
A named human decision is mandatory at each approval step, and the decision record must identify that person.
Every agent output — triage, spread, memo, and compliance exceptions — requires explicit human acceptance before the workflow proceeds to the next stage.
Human reviewers must be able to edit or reject agent output as well as accept it, with the edited/accepted value becoming the system of record and the original draft retained.
Declined deals must require a documented adverse-action reason recorded with the decline decision.
Credit officers must be able to return a deal for rework, sending it back to an earlier stage with a reason and an assignee.
Every state change, ratio calculation, agent draft, and human decision must be written to an immutable audit trail.

The audit trail must be append-only — no update or delete path may be exposed to any user, role, or agent — and each entry must record actor identity, actor type (human or agent), timestamp, deal, event type, and before/after values where applicable.
The audit trail for a deal must be viewable in the UI as a chronological history.
Role-based access control must define a relationship manager role that may submit deals and view only its own deals.
Role-based access control must define a credit analyst role that may spread financials, draft memos, and recommend decisions.
Role-based access control must define a credit officer role that may approve, decline, or return deals for rework.
Relationship manager visibility must be enforced as row-level scoping at the data-access layer, not merely hidden in the UI, and must apply to list views, deal detail, search, and Q&A alike.
Users must authenticate with a persistent named identity, since decisions, acceptances, and audit entries must be attributable to a specific person.
Borrower financial data and application documents must be treated as sensitive: not written to logs or agent telemetry in raw form, and accessible only to users whose role and scope permit it.
An SLA dashboard must surface deals that have been idle past 5 business days.
The system must track a last-activity timestamp per deal and compute idle age using business days (excluding weekends) to drive the SLA dashboard.

Supervision is gates-only: human approval gates are enforced at the defined checkpoints (agent-output acceptance and approval steps) rather than through continuous human supervision of agent execution.
The system must be deployable and runnable on a local target, with no dependency on managed cloud infrastructure for core operation.

Because no supporting documents were supplied, the system must ship with synthetic seed data — sample deals, borrower statements, users in each role, and a default policy rule set — sufficient to demonstrate the full pipeline end to end.

A deal record must be the central entity, holding borrower identity, requested exposure amount, industry, collateral/LTV inputs, current stage, assigned owner, spread, computed ratios, risk grade, memo, exceptions, and decision history.
Each stage must expose a review workspace showing the agent's draft output side by side with its cited sources, so a human can verify before accepting.
The spread view must let a reviewer drill from any figure to the source reference the spreading agent recorded for it.
The portfolio Q&A agent must be reachable through a conversational query interface that displays the supporting deal records behind each answer.
Navigation and available actions must adapt to the signed-in user's role, so each role sees only the deals and controls its permissions allow.

How email applications enter the system is undefined: whether the system connects to a live mailbox (IMAP/API polling) and ingests automatically, or whether a user manually uploads exported email files and attachments. This materially changes intake architecture.
The scope of the final closing stage is undefined: whether it involves generating closing documents, recording funding/booking to a core system, or is simply a terminal status after approval.

data.REQ-017-gap: 5-point scale (1=lowest risk to 5=highest risk) with DSCR ≥1.5→grade 1, 1.25–1.49→grade 2, 1.0–1.24→grade 3, <1.0→grade 4; leverage ≤2.5→reduces grade, >4.0→raises grade by 1; qualitative factors: industry risk adjustment (±1 grade) and management experience (±0.5 grade).
data.REQ-035-gap: Single committee chair approves on behalf of the committee, recording the chair's identity and timestamp; no quorum voting required.
data.REQ-061-gap: Users manually upload exported email files and attachments through a web form, with the system parsing the uploaded file to extract sender, subject, body, and attachments.
data.REQ-062-gap: Terminal status: closing stage records the approval decision and funding date but does not generate documents or post to external systems. The stage exists to mark deals as funded and complete.

workflows.name: deal-underwriting
workflows.description: The end-to-end commercial credit underwriting process: intake and triage, financial spreading, deterministic ratio computation and risk grading, memo drafting, policy compliance review, tiered human approval, and closing — with a mandatory human acceptance gate after every agent draft and a return-for-rework path out of each gate.

nodes.prompt: You are the intake triage agent for deal ${record_intake_deal_id} (borrower ${record_intake_borrower_name}, industry ${record_intake_industry}, requested exposure ${record_intake_requested_amount}). Read ONLY the stored source artifacts ${record_intake_stored_artifact_ids} (email bodies and spreadsheet exports). Classify the request type and product type, judge whether it is suitable for underwriting, list every required document that is missing from the artifacts, and recommend the analyst queue it should be routed to. Do not spread financials, compute ratios, grade risk, or make any decision — that work belongs to other stages. Return a proposal only; a human will accept, edit, or reject it.

nodes.question: Triage proposal for deal ${record_intake_deal_id}: request type ${triage_request_request_type}, product ${triage_request_product_type}, suitable for underwriting = ${triage_request_underwriting_suitable}, missing documents ${triage_request_missing_documents}, recommended queue ${triage_request_recommended_queue}. Accept, edit, reject, or return this deal for rework — and confirm the analyst queue.

nodes.prompt: You are the financial spreading agent for deal ${record_intake_deal_id}. Extract every line item of the standard spread template from the borrower financial statements in artifacts ${record_intake_stored_artifact_ids}. For EVERY figure you emit, attach the source document id, the location within that document (sheet/page, cell/line), and the raw extracted text it came from. Never infer, average, or invent a figure that is not present in a source document — leave it null and say so. Do not compute ratios, assign a grade, or write a memo. Return a proposal only; a human reviewer will accept or edit each figure.

nodes.question: Review the proposed financial spread for deal ${record_intake_deal_id} (${persist_spread_draft_spread_line_item_ids}). Each figure is shown beside the source document and location it was drawn from; unextractable items: ${spread_financials_unextractable_line_item_keys}. Accept, edit the values, reject, or return the deal for rework.

nodes.prompt: You are the credit memo agent for deal ${record_intake_deal_id} (borrower ${record_intake_borrower_name}, industry ${record_intake_industry}, requested exposure ${record_intake_requested_amount}). Draft the underwriting memo using ONLY the accepted spread line items ${apply_spread_decision_accepted_line_item_ids}, the computed ratios DSCR ${compute_ratios_dscr} / leverage ${compute_ratios_leverage} / current ratio ${compute_ratios_current_ratio}, and risk grade ${assign_risk_grade_grade} assigned by rule ${assign_risk_grade_rubric_rule_applied}. Cite the specific ratio ids, spread line item ids, and policy rule ids behind every claim. Do not recompute any ratio, do not change the grade, do not recommend an approval decision. Return a draft only.

nodes.question: Review the drafted credit memo ${persist_memo_draft_memo_draft_id} for deal ${record_intake_deal_id}, shown beside its cited ratios, spread figures, and policy rules. Accept, edit, reject, or return the deal for rework.

nodes.prompt: You are the policy compliance agent for deal ${record_intake_deal_id}. Review the accepted memo ${apply_memo_decision_accepted_memo_id} against the active versioned lending policy rule set, covering at minimum concentration limits (using portfolio exposure ${aggregate_exposure_exposure_by_dimension} and this deal's ${aggregate_exposure_deal_exposure_amount}), prohibited industries (borrower industry: ${record_intake_industry}), and loan-to-value caps (deal LTV: ${record_intake_ltv_percentage}). For each violation raise a written exception naming the policy rule id and describing precisely how the deal breaches it. Do not waive, resolve, or approve anything, and do not alter the memo. Return exceptions only; a human dispositions them.

nodes.question: Deal ${record_intake_deal_id} has ${persist_exceptions_open_exception_count} open policy exception(s) raised against policy version ${policy_review_policy_version}. Disposition each one — accept/waive it with a written reason, mark it resolved, or return the deal for rework.

Deal ${record_intake_deal_id} (${record_intake_borrower_name}, exposure ${derive_approval_tier_exposure_amount}, risk grade ${assign_risk_grade_grade}, DSCR ${compute_ratios_dscr}) requires approval at the ${derive_approval_tier_required_authority_tier} tier. As an authenticated approver at or above that tier, approve, decline (with an adverse-action reason), or return the deal for rework. No agent may make this decision.

workflows.name: portfolio-qa
workflows.description: Read-only portfolio question answering: a credit officer's natural-language question is scoped to the deals their role permits, translated into a structured query, executed deterministically against stored deal data, and answered only from the returned rows with the supporting deal records cited.

nodes.prompt: You are the portfolio Q&A planning agent. Translate the question "${capture_question_question_text}" into a structured READ-ONLY query over deal data (deals, credit_ratios, risk_grades, policy_exceptions, sla_tracking). Emit filters, sort, and the fields to return. You may not write, update, delete, or advance anything, and you may not widen the caller's visibility scope ${resolve_scope_scope_filter} — the query is executed under that scope regardless. If the question cannot be answered from stored deal fields, say so in unanswerable_reason instead of guessing a query.

You are the portfolio Q&A answering agent. Answer "${capture_question_question_text}" using ONLY these ${execute_query_row_count} retrieved rows: ${execute_query_result_rows}. Every figure you state must appear in those rows — never estimate, extrapolate, or mention a deal outside ${execute_query_result_deal_ids}. Cite the deal id behind each figure. If the rows do not support an answer, say exactly that.

workflows.name: sla-escalation
workflows.description: Daily service-level sweep: compute each active deal's business-days idle, flag deals past the 5 business day threshold, summarize the stalled work for a credit officer, and record the officer's escalation decision (reassign, return for rework, or acknowledge) to the audit trail.

nodes.prompt: You are the SLA escalation summary agent. For each deal in ${compute_idle_ages_breaching_deal_ids} (SLA records ${flag_sla_breaches_sla_tracking_ids}), write a one-paragraph summary stating the current stage, the assigned owner, the business days idle, and what the deal is waiting on. Use only stored deal and SLA fields; do not restate borrower financial detail. You may not reassign, advance, or decide anything — propose at most a suggested next action for the credit officer to consider.

nodes.question: ${flag_sla_breaches_breach_count} deal(s) have been idle past 5 business days: ${summarize_breaches_deal_summaries}. For each, decide as credit officer — reassign the owner, return the deal to an earlier stage for rework (with reason and assignee), or acknowledge and leave it in place.
